chunk_findings.detail: The new blocking pip-audit step builds its requirements file with `uv export --locked --no-hashes --no-emit-project` but does not exclude development dependencies. `uv export` includes the default development group unless `--no-dev` or an explicit group filter is used, so the audited set is not the “locked runtime set” promised by the step comment. Given a dev-only dependency such as `pytest` (or another CI-only tool) with a known advisory, `pip-audit --strict` will exit non-zero and fail the quality job even though no shipped runtime package is affected; before this change that same advisory was only a warning because of the removed `|| echo`.
chunk_findings.title: .github/workflows/ci.yml:99

chunk_findings.detail:
`test_pip_audit_is_blocking` only requires the substring `pip-audit` to appear in some non-comment line, so a YAML key satisfies it. A ci.yml step such as:
```yaml
- name: pip-audit
  run: echo "no audit"
```
has a code line `- name: pip-audit`, produces no `|| echo` / `|| true` finding, and then passes the final `assert any("pip-audit" in text ...)`. The test therefore can pass even though no `pip-audit` command is executed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:63

chunk_findings.detail:
The advisory check only inspects a fixed four-code-line window starting at the first line containing `pip-audit`, not the full shell command. For a multi-line invocation like:
```yaml
run: |
  pip-audit \
    --strict \
    --desc \
    --fix \
    --dry-run \
    --output report.json \
    || echo "advisory"
```
the window starting at the `pip-audit \` line stops before `|| echo`, so the test passes even though the audit is advisory.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:59

chunk_findings.detail:
`test_dockerfile_base_images_carry_a_digest` treats every `FROM` target as an external image and flags internal build-stage references. A valid multi-stage Dockerfile such as:
```dockerfile
FROM python:3.13-alpine@sha256:... AS builder
FROM builder AS final
```
fails on the second line because `FROM builder` has no `@sha256:` digest, even though `builder` is a prior stage, not a floating base image.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:78

chunk_findings.detail: `test_lock_file_is_checked_for_drift` searches the raw file text, so the assertion is satisfied by comments or step names containing the command. For example, a ci.yml containing only `# uv lock --check` passes even though no drift-check command is run. The test should use `_code_lines` or a command parser rather than `CI.read_text()`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: The `--with` version check only tests that the captured requirement contains the substring `==`. Input such as `uv run --locked --with bandit==` or `uv run --locked --with bandit==*` passes the test even though no exact version is pinned, contrary to the test’s stated “exact version” contract.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:36

chunk_findings.detail:
`test_pip_audit_is_blocking` uses a sliding window of 4 consecutive code lines to check for `|| echo` or `|| true` after `pip-audit`. In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the dependency audit step spans multiple lines:
```yaml
          uv export --locked --no-hashes --no-emit-project > "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
          uv run --no-project --with pip-audit==2.10.1 pip-audit --strict --progress-spinner off -r "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
          uv run --no-project python scripts/ci/deps-allowlist.py
```
If an error suppression like `|| true` were placed on the `uv export` line or the `deps-allowlist.py` line within the same multi-line run block or step, or if future lines are added between `pip-audit` and an error suppression within a 4-line window, the test fails to inspect the actual execution context correctly or can miss failure-masking operators due to arbitrary line-window slicing. Furthermore, `_code_lines` flattens the file, stripping comments and blank lines, but `lines[i : i + 4]` slices over the filtered code lines rather than logical YAML command blocks, making the window dependent on intervening non-comment lines rather than command boundaries.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:59

chunk_findings.detail:
The new `_logical_commands` parser splits commands on `&&`, so an advisory wrapper can be placed after an `&&` and will no longer be considered part of the pip-audit command. For example, a ci.yml command such as:
```yaml
uv run --no-project --with pip-audit==2.10.1 pip-audit --strict --progress-spinner off -r "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt" && true || echo "advisory"
```
is split into `uv run ... pip-audit ...` and `true || echo ...`. `_pip_audit_commands` returns only the first segment, which has no `||`, so the test passes. Shell `&&`/`||` are left-associative, so if pip-audit fails, the `|| echo` runs and the overall command succeeds, defeating the “blocking pip-audit” requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:test_pip_audit_is_blocking

chunk_findings.detail: This test joins all logical commands into one string and then matches `uv export\b[^|]*--no-dev`, so it can pass when the actual audit export lacks `--no-dev` but the string appears in a step name or another command. For example, a ci.yml step named `- name: uv export --no-dev` followed by an actual `uv export --locked --no-hashes --no-emit-project > req.txt` without `--no-dev` satisfies the assertion, even though the audited requirements file was not exported from the runtime-only set.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:test_pip_audit_audits_the_runtime_set_only

chunk_findings.detail:
The stage-aware check adds the current `FROM ... AS alias` alias to `stages` before testing whether the base image is an internal stage, so a self-referential first stage bypasses the digest requirement. A Dockerfile containing:
```dockerfile
FROM builder AS builder
```
passes because `builder` is inserted into `stages`, then `m.group(1).lower() in stages` is true, even though `builder` was not a previously defined stage and has no `@sha256:` digest.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:test_dockerfile_base_images_carry_a_digest

chunk_findings.detail:
The `--with` regex captures the next whitespace-delimited token including shell quotes, so a valid exact pin such as:
```yaml
uv run --locked --with "bandit==1.7.10"
```
captures `"bandit==1.7.10"` and fails the fullmatch, even though the version is exact. This makes the test reject valid commands.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:test_uv_run_with_tools_carry_an_exact_version

chunk_findings.detail:
This test joins every command in `ci.yml` into one string and only requires some `uv export` to be followed somewhere before a `|` by `--no-dev`. Given a run step such as:
```yaml
uv export --locked --no-hashes --no-emit-project > "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
echo --no-dev
uv run --no-project --with pip-audit==2.10.1 pip-audit --strict -r "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
```
the regex matches the `--no-dev` in the unrelated `echo` line, so the test passes even though the requirements file audited by `pip-audit` was exported without `--no-dev` and may include development dependencies.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:test_pip_audit_audits_the_runtime_set_only

chunk_findings.detail:
The test treats only the presence of `||` as evidence that `pip-audit` is advisory. Given a step such as:
```yaml
run: |
  set +e
  pip-audit --strict -r "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
  set -e
```
`_logical_commands` splits the semicolon-separated commands, `_pip_audit_commands` returns the `pip-audit --strict ...` segment, and `bad` remains empty because that segment has no `||`. The shell suppresses the `pip-audit` exit status under `set +e`, so a high-severity vulnerability does not fail the job, yet the test still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:test_pip_audit_is_blocking

chunk_findings.detail: The drift check only asserts that some command starts with `uv lock --check`; it does not require the command to be blocking. Given `uv lock --check || echo "skip"`, `_logical_commands` does not split on `||`, so `re.match` succeeds and the test passes, while the shell makes the lock-drift check always succeed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:test_lock_file_is_checked_for_drift

chunk_findings.detail: The parser discards an unterminated continuation at end of input. If a run block ends with `uv run --locked --with bandit \` and there is no following code line, the line is accumulated in `pending`, the loop exits, and `return out` never emits it. The exact-version and locked-run tests then see no command and pass despite the unpinned `--with` requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:_logical_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The Dockerfile check adds the `AS` stage name before checking whether the `FROM` target is already a known stage. For `FROM builder AS builder`, `builder` is inserted into `stages` and then the target `builder` is considered internal, so the missing `@sha256:` digest is not reported even though `builder` may be an unpinned registry image; a stage being defined on the current line should not count as already defined.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:test_dockerfile_base_images_carry_a_digest
